clue.text: Bit to eat? Last portion of cheese and pickle

parts.note: a scrap is a small leftover morsel of food

indicators.note: the final portion of the word cheese supplies just its closing letter

explanation.surface: Someone offers a snack: the last bit of cheese with some pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like the chutney beside the cheese, but it is the definition, meaning a tight spot; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an awkward predicament or fix one has got into.

clue.text: A couple of females having to chase around ship's bar

indicators.note: around says the chasing word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to trail is to follow behind, i.e. to chase
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Two women pursue each other around the bar on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having to chase' tempts a solver to put the females behind something; instead 'to chase' supplies the outer word and 'around' wraps it round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the rail around a ship's stern, a bar of wood or metal at the back of the vessel.

clue.text: Suddenly started being arrogant

definitions.meaning: ... as one does when startled, getting to one's feet with a start
... describes someone who has risen above their station and become self-important

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both literally sprang to one's feet and, as an adjective, upstart and conceited.

clue.text: Woman wearing wig the wrong way? Well, maybe

indicators.note: wearing means the woman has the reversed wig around her
the wrong way means the word for wig is turned backwards

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman has put her wig on back to front, a question mark leaving us to wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' is a pronoun here; the definition is a well of the oil kind, flagged by 'maybe' as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is an oil well that spouts freely, so it is an example of a well, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Be off, packing cold ready-cooked chicken

indicators.note: packing says the dismissal word contains the other letters

parts.note: scat is a command meaning go away
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: cooked means the word ready is worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An order to clear off, with a cold ready-cooked chicken stuffed in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready-cooked' splits: 'ready' is the anagram fodder and 'cooked' its signal. 'Chicken' looks like the food but means a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a coward, someone easily frightened.

clue.text: English composer has no tips for singer

indicators.note: has no tips means the composer's name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: William Walton was a twentieth-century English composer

explanation.surface: An English composer is short of money for gratuities, unlike a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no tips' strips W and N off WALTON.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: Can filled with a vegetable dish

indicators.note: filled with says the container word has the other letter put inside it

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A tin is stuffed with a vegetable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled with' puts A inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tian is a Provencal gratin of layered vegetables, named after the earthenware dish it is baked in.

clue.text: Disciple safe after Mass in part of Jerusalem

indicators.note: after puts the safe word behind the rest
in says the mass letter sits inside the hill's name

parts.note: Sion (Zion) is the hill in Jerusalem on which the city was built
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A follower of Jesus keeps safe after going to Mass in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: Sion or Zion, the hill, often stands for Jerusalem itself; 'peter' for a safe is crossword-familiar villains' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Peter is the full name of the apostle Peter, one of the twelve disciples.

clue.text: Badmouthed, say, girls turning very loud after party

indicators.note: after places the very loud marking behind the party
turning means both say and girls are read backwards together

parts.note: eg (for example) is what 'say' means
gals is a casual word for girls
a do is a party
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Some girls are criticised for getting noisy after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' gives its usual crossword sense of 'for example' and is turned along with the girls, giving SLAGGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag off is British slang for to criticise someone harshly behind their back.

clue.text: Top set lacks energy to prepare for exam

indicators.note: lacks says the energy letter is removed

parts.note: the cream is the best group, the top set
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: The top set in a school lacks the energy to revise for a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' drops E from CREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to study intensively just before a test.

clue.text: Some herbal medication that will soothe the skin

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy that calms the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'herbal medication'.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm is a soothing ointment applied to sore or irritated skin.

clue.text: Attractive place refurbished in past? You bet

indicators.note: refurbished means these letters are done up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A betting tip that a scenic spot has been done up in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' rearranges PAST YOU BET; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a scenic location people visit for its looks.

clue.text: One in the main is quite right to conceal trouble

indicators.note: to conceal says the other letters hide the trouble word

parts.note: so can mean quite or very
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone mostly right about hiding a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the open sea, a poetic usage; 'quite' for SO, as in 'it is so true'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is someone on the main, an old word for the open ocean.

clue.text: Savages gathered near large US city

indicators.note: gathered means the letters of savages are collected into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild people have assembled near a large American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' rearranges SAVAGES; 'near' is a link putting L beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is a city in Nevada, USA, famous for its casinos.

clue.text: Ambassador travels beyond British isles

indicators.note: beyond places the travel word after the British letter

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
rides means travels

explanation.surface: A diplomat journeys out past British islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' puts RIDES after B.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are the island groups off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Preacher we agreed should retire about fifty

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the fifty
should retire means the agreement word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: yes expresses agreement
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A churchman we all agreed ought to retire at about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should retire' turns YES into SEY; 'about' puts it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wesley was the eighteenth-century preacher who founded Methodism.

clue.text: Old leader an ill-bred fellow, mostly, and cold

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a churl is a rude, ill-mannered man
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A former head of state dismissed as a coarse fellow, and a cold one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' docks the L from CHURL; 'an' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's wartime prime minister, a leader of the past.

clue.text: Foremost among remedies if in a tizzy?

definitions.text: Foremost among remedies if in a tizzy?

indicators.note: in puts those opening letters inside the tizzy word

parts.note: a spin is a state of agitation, a tizzy

indicators.note: foremost among takes the opening letters of remedies and if

explanation.surface: The top remedy when you are in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foremost among' gives R and I, which 'in' puts inside A SPIN. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is a leading remedy taken for headaches brought on by stress.

clue.text: Decline to turn up for festival

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to die can mean to decline or fade away

explanation.surface: Refusing to attend a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses DIE. 'Decline' looks like refusing an invitation but means wither.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid is a Muslim religious festival, such as Eid al-Fitr at the end of Ramadan.

clue.text: What to wear when it's sunny: constant subject for discussion

parts.words: What to wear when it's sunny
parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, worn against strong sunshine
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Sunny weather wear is a perennial thing to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPI (or topee) is the pith helmet once worn in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter talked about.

clue.text: Struggling to become really healthy

parts.note: fighting means struggling
fit, as in befit, means to suit or become, as in 'that dress becomes you'

explanation.surface: Battling hard to get into top condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become' is in its sense of suit, as clothes become someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting fit is an idiom for being in excellent physical condition.

clue.text: Queen going over area such as Sandringham, say, again

indicators.note: going over puts the queen letter on top in this down clue

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
Sandringham, the royal country house in Norfolk, stands on a large estate

explanation.surface: The Queen touring Sandringham, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandringham is a private royal estate in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to say something once more.

clue.text: Kiddies, note, regularly deleted image on screen

indicators.note: regularly deleted means every other letter of the two words is dropped

explanation.surface: Children and a music note are cut out of a picture on the TV.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of KIDDIES NOTE leaves the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An ident is the short logo sequence a TV channel shows between programmes.

clue.text: In pieces, being thrown out of club?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as un-membered, having one's membership removed

explanation.definitionFit: Dismembered means torn limb from limb, and humorously suggests stripped of club membership.

clue.text: American promoted over Chinese statesman

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means the word is raised, reading upwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A US official has been advanced over a Chinese leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns AM to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Zedong was the communist leader who founded the People's Republic of China.

clue.text: Detailed talk publicly supporting English political party

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the speech word beneath the others

parts.note: Lab is short for the British Labour Party
to orate is to make a public speech

explanation.surface: A thorough public speech backing an English party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts ORATE under E LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and full of detail.

clue.text: Good walk? Run's better

parts.note: to amble is to walk leisurely
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Is a good stroll better than a run?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative but means one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A better (bettor) is one who bets, i.e. a punter.

clue.text: Overprotects lettuce plants

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce
to set is to plant

explanation.surface: A gardener mollycoddles the lettuce plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or coddle excessively.

clue.text: Mother lifted covering off lounge floor

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: covering off means its first letter is removed

parts.note: to laze is to lounge

explanation.surface: Mum lifts the cover off the lounge floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns MA to AM; 'covering off' takes L from LAZE. 'Floor' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to stun or astonish them.

clue.text: Size of paper once used for maps

definitions.text: Size of paper once used for maps

parts.words: Size of paper once used for maps
parts.note: a large old paper format, named after the bound books of maps it was used for

explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was a large paper size, named for the bound map books it was used for.

clue.text: Caught sight of gnome

definitions.meaning: a gnome is a pithy maxim or proverb, an old saying

explanation.definitionFit: Saw is the past tense of see and also an old proverb or adage.
